title: Pharmacy engine test vectors
description: Machine-readable test vectors transcribed from the research notes. Published numbers are copied verbatim (raw cell text is kept next to every parsed number). See docs/ENGINE-SPEC.md section 14.

basis.description: Why this tolerance: the note's suggested tolerance, published rounding, or machine precision.

kind.description: worked_example: published inputs and published output. derived_check: analytic value computed by the research team (labelled DERIVED in the note). property: an invariant to test with property-based tests. dataset: measured observations for validation. rule: a regulatory rule with its worked values.

target.description: Dotted name of the engine function the vector exercises (for example pharmacy.exposure.mean_kinetic_temperature), or 'oracle:<name>' for a tests/oracle helper, or null for validation datasets consumed by tests/validation.

inputs.description: Free-form JSON. Units are spelled in key names (for example temperatures_c, k_per_min).

expected.description: Values the test asserts, in the units named by the keys. For datasets: the observations.

published_expected_text.description: Verbatim published wording of the expected output, when there is one.

our_recomputation.description: The research team's recomputation, as stated in the note.

source_status.description: Status label copied from the note (read, abstract, cited-only, READ, READ (abstract), CITED, DERIVED, computed).

status.description: reproduces: the note's recomputation matches the published value within the tolerance (worked examples), or the dataset's internal summaries agree with its raw values as far as the note checked. known_mismatch: the note documents a disagreement; tests must assert the documented behaviour, never tune the engine to the published number. unverified: the inputs or recomputation are not available in the notes (for example the dataset lives outside the repository).
